summary: Post-deploy prefetch eviction + mixed-quant profile triggered elevated 5xxs and throughput drop — guidance for controlled exit preserving tenant state
description: Issue summary: After a scheduled optimizer profile swap for tenant NexCommerce on 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC, we observed a spike in 5xx responses from the inference endpoint and a concurrent throughput regression for the tenant. Impact: ~18% of requests for this tenant returned 5xx over a 25-minute window; p95 latency increased from 210ms to 1.2s. This tenant is on Dedicated capacity; auto-scaling did not immediately mitigate. They are reporting production user-facing errors. We need guidance to perform a controlled exit of the new mixed-quant + prefetch profile while preserving session/kv state and avoiding mass evictions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Tenant traffic routed to dedicated pool with optimizer-profile: mixed-quant-prefetch-v3
2) Trigger standard chat generation workload (short prompts, multi-turn) at 200 qps per-tenant shard
3) Observe serving runtime logs: increased kv eviction churn and 5xx errors (model load/cache miss path)
4) p95 and throughput regressions appear within ~3-5 minutes of deploy
observed_behavior: p95 latency regressed to 1.2s from baseline 210ms
throughput for tenant fell ~25% despite available GPU headroom
kv-cache eviction rate spiked and latency for first token increased
expected_behavior: No increase in 5xx error rate after optimizer profile change
Throughput and latency within 10% of baseline for same workload
Graceful fallback to compatible model variant or demotion path without tenant disruption
logs: [2026-03-12T02:03:14Z] serving-runtime ERROR tenant=nexcommerce request_id=3ff2b6 5xx model= gptx-7b-quantized-v2 kernel-failure: kv-evict-throttle
[2026-03-12T02:10:21Z] optimizer INFO profile-swap applied tenant=nexcommerce old=quant-v1 new=mixed-quant-prefetch-v3
[2026-03-12T02:15:07Z] api-gateway ERROR upstream 502 connection-reset by peer
temporary_mitigation: 1) Temporarily pinned tenant to previous model variant (gptx-7b-fp16) via routing override
2) Throttled tenant to 150 qps to reduce eviction churn while we investigate
3) Enabled extended kv-cache TTL for the tenant as an emergency measure
investigation_notes: - Initial hypothesis: mixed-quant layout interacts with prefetch/eviction heuristic causing aggressive KV eviction under short-turn workloads.
- Observed that prefetch triggered a wave of large KV allocations which evicted critical prefixes; next requests hit model cold path causing 5xx on kernel memory allocation failures.
- Autoscale did not kick synchronous with error window: scheduler delay and queueing contributed to client-facing 5xx.
- No changes to infra (nodes) at time of incident beyond profile flip; related PR referenced for optimizer heuristics (runtime PR #2145).
- Reproducer: synthetic replay at 180-220 qps with multi-turn prompts reproduces eviction/5xx pattern locally in staging with identical profile.
analysis: Root cause likely a resource allocation mismatch between mixed-quant kernel memory expectations and the prefetch eviction policy threshold.
Mixed-quant kernels have different KV sizing; prefetch assumed FP16 sizes and over-allocated internal buffers leading to eviction storms.
Edge-case: tenant workload has very short sequences with many small turns, which exacerbates thrash when prefetch pulls longer contexts.
Recommendation: coordinated demotion path that disables prefetch first and then rolls back quant profile rather than switching both at once.
proposed_action_plan: A) Orchestrated safe-exit steps we can run for NexCommerce:
1) Schedule a short maintenance window (5 mins) and enable routing pin to previous model variant to stop new sessions entering mixed profile.
2) Disable prefetch feature flag for tenant (config: optimizer.prefetch.enabled=false) to stop further KV prefetch allocations.
3) Drain existing prefetch allocations: run kv-evict-sweep with tenant-safe mode to free non-critical prefixes, preserving active sessions' prefixes.
4) After evictions stabilize, roll model variant back to fp16 baseline and monitor p95/5xx for 15 minutes.
5) If stable, gradually lift throttles and remove routing pin.
B) If above fails to restore within 30 minutes, follow emergency fallback: disable optimizer profile entirely for tenant and escalate to SRE for node-level memory allocation tracing.
questions_for_customer: 1) Can NexCommerce accept a 5-minute maintenance window now (ETA to start provided)?
2) Are there any session-affinity constraints or long-running sessions we must preserve?
3) Do they have any traffic spikes scheduled in next 2 hours?
comments: 2026-03-12 02:28 - Ava Thompson (Support): Acknowledged. We've pinned tenant routing to previous variant and applied 150 qps throttle while we prepare an action plan.
2026-03-12 03:05 - Liam Chen (SRE): Reproducer verified in staging. Prefetch allocations spike shortly after mixed-quant profile engages. Logging attached to PR #2145 for kernel sizing mismatch.
2026-03-12 04:10 - Customer (NexCommerce - S. Patel): We see user-facing errors on checkout flows. Please prioritize. We can take a short maintenance window.
2026-03-13 09:12 - Liam Chen (SRE): Drafted safe-exit plan above. Requesting approval to disable prefetch for tenant and perform controlled kv-evict-sweep. ETA to start: 10 minutes after approval.
2026-03-14 01:20 - Product (Maya Rivera): Note: optimizer team will follow up with a long-term fix to prefetch sizing heuristics; linking an internal ticket INT-4382.

2026-03-14 08:45 - Liam Chen (SRE): Proceeded with staged exit at 2026-03-14T08:30Z: prefetch disabled, kv-evict-sweep run in safe mode, routing pin removed after 20m of stable metrics. Monitoring continues.
resolution: Action taken: Safely disabled prefetch for tenant, performed targeted kv-evict-sweep preserving active prefixes, rolled routing back to fp16 variant, removed throttles after stabilization.
Result: 5xx rate returned to baseline within 12 minutes of pinned rollback; p95 latency returned to ~230ms. Throughput restored to expected levels.

Follow-up: Engineering will publish an optimizer patch to correct prefetch sizing assumptions for mixed-quant kernels (tracked in INT-4382). Recommend staged rollout and tenant simulator preflight (templates attached).
Customer confirmation: NexCommerce verified checkout flows are healthy. Customer asked for runbook steps to avoid flip of quant+prefetch together in future.
follow_up_tasks: 1) Create preflight check that rejects simultaneous quant-profile + prefetch toggles for dedicated tenants (owner: optimizer team).
2) Add a suggested maintenance checklist to Console UI when applying optimizer profile changes to Dedicated pools.
3) Coordinate a rolling test with NexCommerce in staging using tenant-simulator (task assigned INT-4382).
